criteria.rationale: The general retryBeforeAccept statement quantifies over every budget flag and returns retry on the unvalidated branch.

The existing general invalid-evidence no-op and unvalidated-address preservation prevent invalid validation. Module 77 has a real authority-granting authentication transition, with general accepted and rejected complete-state statements. Its arbitrary mixed-trace erasure theorem and identity and privilege projections prove that reachability evidence alone never changes either authority flag. General post-authentication reachability traces retain exactly the verified identity and gated privilege; the result does not rely on an absence of modeled authority grants.

obligations.scope_review: R03 turn 5 closes both frozen M007 criteria. Module 80 composes arbitrary finite swarm/source/identity populations and weighted resource dimensions, with honest, worker, reconnect and distributed roles, under one explicitly supplied host vector. Connection and reconnect-burst parameters are member counts, bank weights and bank capacities in this arbitrary fleet. Each honest peer, connection, worker or reconnecting peer can be a separate member with its own banks. Traces keep the member population fixed for one interval. A burst in that interval is any finite trace of hostEvent and hostChurn steps. M013 owns burst-plus-rate budgets across intervals. Indexed ownership transitions and identity churn preserve every slice. Per-interval clipped work demands share the same aggregate allocation condition. Runtime routing, storage/work dominance and work-budget enforcement remain external premises. External obligation E022 owns established-resource routing and enforcement of the measured whole-process budget across all identities, connection directions and swarms. External obligation E013 owns runtime pending accounting within the same whole-process budget. External obligation E010 owns production calibration and deployed storage and work dominance. Source normalization and resource-specific vectors remain M003/M009/M012 work.

criteria.rationale: hostFleetBound and sharedHostTraceBound quantify over an arbitrary finite population and every resource coordinate. The total allocated weight includes every honest/worker/reconnect/distributed member and every supplied swarm/source/identity. hostFleetWorkBound and sharedHostWorkAfterTraceBound compose arbitrary clipped work demands under the same sum-of-slices host premise. Complete-state equations pin routing and head/suffix accounting.

Every distributed identity/prefix occurrence contributes its own slice to hostFleetAllocation; equal labels and labels that churn assigns receive no independent host budget. hostFleetRelabelAllocation and hostFleetRelabelUse retain allocations and charges through arbitrary relabeling. No module-80 definition reads a role, swarm, source or identity label. These equalities follow because relabeling keeps the bank vector. The controls host_churn_resets_banks and host_churn_duplicates_slice reject changes to that definition. HostTrace has no join step, so membership is fixed during the interval. A new source needs a new aggregate-fit witness. M012 owns grants that change the population. M013 owns distinct-source and aggregate burst budgets for handshake starts. hostTraceAllocation and sharedHostTraceBound extend this fact to arbitrary mixed ownership/churn traces, and the work bounds include all member demands. Mutation controls reject omitted participants, duplicated slices and charge-resetting churn.

criteria.rationale: The recorded general trace bounds and ownership transitions establish this criterion under the explicit shared-bank, atomicity and runtime domination premises. Fixed-slot semantic witnesses retain their stated generation/index limits.

In the model, every endpoint and swarm event uses one waiting bank and one active bank. No event reads its endpoint field, so each endpoint charge is part of the same occupancy. No endpoint gets a private copy of the allocation. executorHostResourceTraceBound bounds the summed weighted charge of both banks by the single initial host allocation for every finite trace. executorEventWorkBound bounds the work of each event by the host event budget. executorHostWorkTraceBound bounds the work of every finite trace by its event count times that budget. executorSingletonWorkCharged and executorZeroDemandStillCharges show that each event keeps its charge, also at zero demand. The model has no per-endpoint quota. Composition depends on the recorded shared-bank routing premise. E019 owns this premise: its criterion 1 requires process-wide composition and an explicit M011 refinement. Traces permit every finite interleaving. The only ordering premise is that each reservation, transfer and terminal release is atomic. No witness uses the removed accept/endpoint mutex, a serialization premise or a fairness premise.

obligations.scope_review: Turn 15 reviews all four frozen M012 criteria as witnessed. Modules 86-89 retain finite peer/swarm vector grants, churn/exemption accounting, generation-owned release, arbitrary-position coupled stage promotion/refusal and separate advertised-credit/resident domination. The criterion-1 rationale retains the limitation that establishedTraceKeepsOtherPhases alone does not witness stage accounting. Module 90 closes criterion 2 with occupied-slot workload certificates, guarded all-peer FIFO transitions, funded delivered ticks and complete critical-plus-coupled process composition, including separate shared overhead. No desired service result is a premise. The captured-window assumptions retain static protected ownership and eligibility while arbitrary bulk/pending/pre-accept schedules run in their disjoint allocation. All dimensions, protocol directions, peers and swarm labels remain represented. The separation of bulk events from the critical fleet and the static critical banks hold by construction of module 90. They are premises for the runtime and earn no noninterference credit. Runtime routing, nonaliasing, atomicity, authority, cost domination, resource termination and scheduler conformance remain explicit E010/E013/E017/E019/E021/E022 obligations.

criteria.rationale: One fixed owned population supplies grants in both directions for connections, QUIC streams and advertised receive credit, request-response, negotiating/Kademlia substreams, bytes and tasks. Arbitrary mixed resource/churn traces preserve all vector bounds across trust and swarm labels, with explicit routing and initial-fit premises.

Modules 86-89 distinguish pending handshakes, pre-accept executor work and established resources in one coupled process. Established release/shedding isolates its selected generation-owned allocation. No established event of module 86 can change the pending lease pool or the pre-accept work field. As a result, establishedTraceKeepsOtherPhases holds by construction and does not witness stage accounting. Nonpromotion transitions preserve the other stages. Promotion success is derived from a held pending generation and a vacant established generation at arbitrary pending, peer, bank and slot prefixes/suffixes, with no assumed promotion guard. Its complete-state equation frees only the selected pending generation (consuming it), acquires only the selected established generation, preserves the executor, and retains every unselected prefix and suffix. Complete-state refusal covers every absent pending/member/bank/slot index, free pending ownership, any explicitly mismatched generation and occupied destinations at arbitrary positions. Generation consumption, replay idempotence, established release isolation and arbitrary mixed-trace stage allocation bounds remain witnessed. Runtime classification/routing, atomicity, receipt authority, actual resource termination and cost domination remain explicit external obligations; critical scheduling service remains criterion 2.

Module 90 requires each finite FIFO prefix to fit occupied established protocol slots and a common maximum. It derives all-peer service from continuous eligibility, full-population round funding and enough delivered ticks. The service derivation uses the rank bound; the occupied-slot certificate is a workload premise. The schedule projects bulk events through the existing coupled process and critical ticks through guarded FIFO transitions. No bulk event can change the critical fleet, and no critical tick can change a bank. As a result, protectedBulkCannotSteal, protectedBulkStep, protectedResourcesPreserved, protectedWidthPreserved and protectedCriticalBound hold by construction and do not witness runtime noninterference or critical grant and release accounting. Separation of bulk and critical work is a premise. All peers and arbitrary swarm labels contribute to the critical resource vector and round cost. Critical banks remain charged throughout the window, while pending, pre-accept and bulk resources use a disjoint coupled allocation. Whole-process and explicit overhead bounds apply to the same mixed schedules, with actual cost domination and initial coordinate-wise fit. The tick premise counts delivered ticks. The model treats each funded delivered tick as one completed FIFO round for each eligible peer, as in module 35. No premise asserts target service. Runtime scheduler, routing, nonaliasing and cost conformance remain E010/E013/E017/E019/E021/E022 obligations.

Advertised credit has an exact independent coordinate and cannot alter reserved or actual symbolic resident unit costs. Explicit per-slot byte/task domination certificates lift through all banks and peers into arbitrary-trace process resident bounds. Fixed/shared resident overhead has separate domination and reserved capacity, charged even with zero occupied slots. Runtime costs must refine these supplied upper bounds.

obligations.scope_review: R03 turn 6 closes both frozen M021 criteria. Module 81 models listener/dial endpoints and all swarms in one generation-indexed routing table. An identifier selects one cell; distinct-slot update laws prevent cross-connection changes. Validated, generation-matching migration changes the destination while preserving the original owner. Handshake success retains established routing, while every terminal outcome removes the matching route and advances its generation before reuse. Unvalidated, mismatched and repeated-vacant callbacks preserve complete cells. Arbitrary finite schedules preserve capacity, bound live and discarded state separately, and conserve their sum. No fairness premise is used. E019 retains concrete callback authority, destination validation, serialization, generation/storage refinement and transport regression obligations.

criteria.rationale: The exact five-source constructor, current Closed acceptance/refusal and Open-default witnesses quantify every role and primary/worker index. Targeted verified updates, arbitrary worker prefix/suffix preservation, worker-list extension (existing workers kept, every other new index empty) and complete-state provisional trace preservation cover the general update scope. All 34 controls are linked by canonical hashes. Authentication/source verification and operator authority remain granted model premises; runtime derivation and M023 lifecycle enforcement receive no credit here.

Failure branches are explicit. authoritativeClosedUnlistedRefused refuses an identity that is absent from the selected union in a Closed view, for either authentication flag. authoritativeUnionRequiresIdentity refuses an unauthenticated identity with no profile hypothesis. unverifiedCommitteeUpdateIsNoOp keeps the complete policy for every flag-off update. everyProvisionalUnionTraceIsNoOp keeps the complete policy for every finite provisional trace. missingWorkerUnionIsEmpty returns the empty union for every index of the empty worker list. workerExtensionKeepsExistingWorkers keeps every existing worker when an update extends the worker list. paddedWorkerUnionIsEmpty and workerBeyondExtensionIsEmpty return the empty union for every other new index when an update extends the empty worker list. Conditional premises are explicit. The Closed, Open and Grace statements carry the displayed profile equality. The listed and absent statements carry the displayed membership equality. The six authoritative query statements bind every role, swarm, policy value and identity index. The six committee update statements bind every role, swarm, incoming union and policy value. The three arbitrary_trace statements bind every finite change list and policy value. unionTraceAppliesFirstChangeFirst binds every change, remaining change list and policy value. The other module-91 statements are component statements with narrower binders. The two module-33 flat-list statements keep local credit only. The authentication flag, faithful identity indexing, verified initial membership vectors, the verification flag and authorized operator configuration are granted model premises. E029 owns their runtime derivation. M023 owns lifecycle enforcement.

obligations.scope_review: R04 turn 2: module 92 implements distinct inbound admission, outbound dial and outbound establishment transitions for every node role, primary and arbitrary-index worker swarm. Inbound/dial decisions use the current exact authoritative union; establishment checks generation, role, swarm and identity and independently re-queries the current authenticated policy. Closed, Open and Grace behavior is preserved explicitly. Mixed finite update traces advance generation by their exact effective update count. A prior receipt remains refused after a verified roster or authorized profile update and any following mixed trace. An executable exchange places arbitrary prefix/intervening changes around separate dial/establishment decisions, rejects every intervening trace with a positive effective revision count and also has a positive fresh-success witness. The old module-33 statements keep only their recorded local credit. Atomic current-authority capture, faithful indexing/current authentication, correctly classified roster updates, authorized profile events and unbounded model generations are explicit premises. M024 retains independent bounded privileges and M040 retains live-connection sweeps; E029 retains runtime receipt provenance, publication, generation persistence and refinement. The sealed obligation and external boundary are unchanged.

criteria.rationale: Distinct executable lifecycle transitions use the current authority and bind establishment to its revision/context. The cited general and arbitrary-trace witnesses cover every role/swarm, actual intervening updates, explicit Open/Grace fallback, authentication, stale refusals and fresh success. Module-33 witnesses retain only local supplied-snapshot credit; runtime receipt provenance/publication remain E029 and independent bounded privileges/live-connection sweeps remain M024/M040 as recorded in scope_review.

Failure branches are explicit. allUnionLifecyclePointsRequireIdentity refuses an unauthenticated identity at each of the three lifecycle points. inboundUnionChecksCurrent and outboundUnionDialChecksCurrent equate the inbound and dial allowed flags with the current authoritative query, so a denied query gives no approval. refusedUnionDialCannotEstablish refuses establishment after a refused dial. mismatchedUnionGeneration, mismatchedUnionRole, mismatchedUnionSwarm and mismatchedUnionIdentity turn the receipt match off when the generation, role, swarm or identity comparison is off. mismatchedUnionRevisionCannotEstablish refuses establishment for every receipt whose match is off. deniedCurrentUnionCannotEstablish and unauthenticatedUnionCannotEstablish refuse establishment on a denied or unauthenticated current query, for every receipt. unionChangesGeneration shows that a trace advances the generation by its count of verified roster updates and profile changes only, so provisional roster events consume no revision. advancedUnionReceiptAfterTraceCannotEstablish and selectedUnionDialAfterAdvanceCannotEstablish refuse a receipt captured before one generation advance, for every finite following trace. verifiedUnionUpdateAndTraceCannotEstablish and unionProfileUpdateAndTraceCannotEstablish refuse a prior receipt after a verified roster update or a profile update, for every finite following trace. unionOutboundExchangeAfterVerifiedUpdateRefused refuses the executable exchange when a verified update is the first intervening event, for every prefix trace and every following trace. unionOutboundExchangeAfterEffectiveChangesRefused refuses the exchange for every intervening trace with a positive effective revision count. Together the statements quantify over every node role, the primary swarm and every worker index, every policy value, every identity index and every finite mixed trace. Conditional premises are explicit: atomic capture of the current authority, faithful identity indexing, current authentication, correctly classified roster updates, authorized profile events, unbounded generations and each Equal premise in the recorded statements. Module-33 witnesses keep local supplied-snapshot credit only. E029 keeps runtime receipt provenance, publication and generation persistence. M024 keeps independent bounded privileges. M040 keeps live-connection sweeps.

obligations.scope_review: R04 turn 3 closes the independent bounded privilege obligation. Module 93 represents admission, retention/mesh preference and load-penalty exemption as separately selected finite recipient allocations. Six actual-event noninterference theorems and exact selected-update witnesses separate the classes. Every effective query requires current authentication and membership in the current authoritative role/swarm union of previous/current/next committee, configured trusted and bootstrap identities. All finite mixed revisions preserve those gates, finite allocation bounds, genuine protocol-violation bans and supplied CPU/memory/bulk service-turn limits. Successful and refused paths are witnessed. Recipient capacities are fixed query parameters. No modeled event revises them; E029 owns runtime capacity selection and versioning. These are reserved per-service limits; aggregate reservation and cost domination retain the M012/E022 boundary. Existing module-30 scalar statements retain their narrower scope. Startup/redial, live sweeps and other R04 obligations are not credited.

criteria.rationale: Separate finite recipient lists and limits, exact class selectors, authorized selected updates, all six effective-query noninterference directions and positive/negative query branches establish the three-way bounded privilege split for arbitrary roles, swarms and identities. Current authority changes may intentionally affect eligibility across classes; changing one allocation cannot silently change another allocation or effective privilege.

R04 turn 3 closes the independent bounded privilege obligation. Module 93 represents admission, retention/mesh preference and load-penalty exemption as separately selected finite recipient allocations. Six actual-event noninterference theorems and exact selected-update witnesses separate the classes.
